selection: Lowest physical armMSE over registered200 held-out frames, across parent and250/500-update checkpoints of both branches. Ties prefer fewer optimizer updates, then alphabetical branch label. Parent stays selected if neither branch improves. Robot rollouts are later diagnostics and never choose weights.
hypothesis: Resetting full-decoder training to higher learning rates may disrupt the useful parent; a ten-times lower shared rate scale may preserve or improve held-out commands. This is tested within identical local branches, not against different cloud hardware or batching.
limits: Single seed and coupled global learning-rate scales; cannot isolate decoder versus head rates. Native microbatch schedule is twice optimizer update counts. Engineering weights excluded, originalRSI/r1/query untouched, no new paid jobs or rentals. No control or final-acceptance claim from offline errors. Sequential execution may affect timing; no latency claim from training wall time.
